question.problem: Suppose that $f(x)=2x+6$ and $g(x)=\frac{x}{2}+k.$ If $g$ is the inverse of $f,$ then $k=$
question.worked_solution:
If $g$ is the inverse of $f,$ then we must have:

$$
g(f(x))=x
$$

To find $g(f(x)),$ we write down the function $g$ and replace every occurrence of $x$ with $f(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}g(x) & =\frac{x}{2}+k \\ g(f(x)) & =\frac{f(x)}{2}+k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $f(x)=2x+6$ into the right-hand side of our expression and simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(f(x)) & =\frac{f(x)}{2}+k \\  & =\frac{2x+6}{2}+k \\  & =x+3+k\end{aligned}
$$

However, we also know that $g(f(x))=x.$ Equating the expression above with $x$ and solving for $k$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+3+k & =x \\ \cancel{x}+3+k & =\cancel{x} \\ 3+k & =0 \\ k & =-3\end{aligned}
$$
